Feature lines of surfaces and meshes

Source: R/outline-3d.R
outline_3d.Rd

outline_3d() describes the lines a surface or mesh layer derives from its own triangles, passed as its outline argument: silhouettes, where the surface turns away from the camera, creases, where neighbouring faces meet at a sharp angle, and boundaries, the edges of open surfaces (Bénard and Hertzmann 2019). They are drawn as strokes of the scene, so they are hidden by nearer surfaces like any other line, and hidden chooses whether their hidden parts are left out, dashed or drawn.

Usage

outline_3d(
  silhouette = TRUE,
  crease = 30,
  boundary = TRUE,
  colour = "black",
  linewidth = 0.5,
  linetype = 1,
  alpha = 1,
  hidden = c("hide", "dashed", "show"),
  halo = NULL
)

Arguments

silhouette

TRUE, FALSE, "smooth" or "mesh".

crease

Crease angle in degrees, or NULL for no creases.

boundary

Whether to draw boundary edges.

colour, linewidth, linetype, alpha

Stroke of the lines.

hidden

Hidden stroke policy of the lines: "hide", "dashed" or "show".

halo

Width of the gap left on each side of a line where farther lines pass behind it: a physical grid::unit() or a number in millimetres. NULL (the default) for no gap.

Value

An outline specification for the outline argument of geom_surface_3d(), geom_mesh_3d() and the surface stats.

Details

An edge is a boundary when it belongs to one triangle and a crease when the normals of its two triangles differ by more than crease degrees. Silhouettes depend on the view and are recomputed from the panel's camera when the plot is built. On a mesh (silhouette = "mesh") they are the edges between a triangle facing the camera and one facing away; they follow the edges, so they zigzag across a finely curved surface. On a smooth surface (silhouette = "smooth") they are the interpolated contours of Hertzmann and Zorin (2000): the zero set of n . (c - p), the vertex normal against the direction to the camera, interpolated linearly along each edge, which crosses the faces as a smooth curve. Because that curve lies on the triangles a little inside the mesh's own outline, nearer triangles can hide short pieces of it. silhouette = TRUE takes the smooth contour for layers with vertex normals (nx, ny, nz, as grid, parametric and isosurface layers have) and the mesh silhouette otherwise. In the interactive viewer, silhouettes stay those of the initial camera.

halo draws haloed lines (Appel, Rohlf and Stein 1979): each feature line masks a band of the given width on both sides of its stroke, and any line behind it is cut back inside that band, so a line passing behind another stops short of it instead of touching it. The stroke itself stays linewidth wide. The band only cuts lines lying farther from the camera, never faces, and lines that end at a common vertex, such as the edges at a corner of a cube, still meet there.

References

Appel, Rohlf and Stein (1979). The haloed line effect for hidden line elimination. SIGGRAPH '79. https://history.siggraph.org/?p=104577

Bénard and Hertzmann (2019). Line drawings from 3D models: a tutorial. Foundations and Trends in Computer Graphics and Vision 11, 1-159. doi:10.1561/0600000075

Hertzmann and Zorin (2000). Illustrating smooth surfaces. SIGGRAPH 2000, 517-526. doi:10.1145/344779.345074

Examples

torus <- function(u, v) list(x = (1 + 0.4 * cos(v)) * cos(u),
  y = (1 + 0.4 * cos(v)) * sin(u), z = 0.4 * sin(v))
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  geom_parametric_3d(fun = torus, n = c(48, 24), closed = TRUE, fill = "white",
    outline = outline_3d(linewidth = 0.8)) +
  coord_3d()
cube <- expand.grid(x = 0:1, y = 0:1, z = 0:1)
quads <- rbind(c(1, 3, 4, 2), c(5, 6, 8, 7), c(1, 2, 6, 5), c(3, 7, 8, 4),
  c(1, 5, 7, 3), c(2, 4, 8, 6))
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  geom_mesh_3d(vertices = cube, faces = quads, fill = "grey90",
    outline = outline_3d(hidden = "dashed")) +
  coord_3d()
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  geom_parametric_3d(fun = torus, n = c(48, 24), closed = TRUE, fill = "white",
    outline = outline_3d(crease = NULL, hidden = "show", halo = grid::unit(1, "mm"))) +
  coord_3d(elevation = 30)
